scope.task: production device debug interface authority and per-device credential lifecycle
covers: debug interface authority (SWD, UART, ROM USB) under normal and temporary physical possession
communications and peripherals at the device endpoint
credential provisioning, rotation, revocation, reset, RMA and decommission
adjacentSkillsNotCovered: applied-cryptography owns algorithm and protocol construction; the authored policy records algorithmOwnedBy as applied-cryptography and no algorithm is evaluated here.
embedded-firmware owns RTOS tasks, drivers and peripheral implementation; this artifact records the security invariants those mechanisms must enforce.
supply-chain-security owns build provenance, dependency and release-signing trust; this artifact records whether the device accepts the right artifact.
infrastructure-security / cloud-security own the fleet backend; this artifact owns the device endpoint and its trust boundary.
threat-modeling-practice may establish the broader threat model; this artifact converts device-specific threats into enforceable controls.

vocabulary.hardware-observed: read off the representative board and recorded in the supplied corpus (corpus.observed), or a register read the fixture contract states was taken on that board
vocabulary.documentation: supplied by the fixture README, the device-data-sheet policy it describes, or the authored production policy in .kory-eval/device-config.json; not a measurement
vocabulary.simulation: computed by the supplied src/device-sim.ts state machine or by this repository's own lifecycle model; proves state-machine logic, not silicon behaviour

labels.rule: every factual section carries an evidenceLabel; a simulation or documentation label means the property was not measured on hardware

alternatives: a product bound to another device class
resolvedFacts.decision: product is device-x: the wrong-product corpus image is rejected on product binding, not on signature
resolvedFacts.consequence: a signed image for another product would be accepted if product binding were disabled, because its signature is valid

alternatives: a development or test key-hash record
resolvedFacts.decision: the trust anchor is the recorded production key-hash record prod-key-hash-2026
resolvedFacts.consequence: a development anchor would accept images signed with a key the fleet never issued for this product

resolvedFacts.decision: minimumVersion=7, the version of the board-observed deployed image (current@7)
resolvedFacts.consequence: the correctly signed older image (older@5) is rejected as a rollback; with minimumVersion=5 it would boot, which is the downgrade the policy exists to stop

resolvedFacts.fact: debug lock and physical fuse proof
alternatives: claiming the lock register proves physical enforcement
resolvedFacts.decision: the production lock register value is recorded as board-observed, while debug-lock and physical-fuse enforcement are recorded as unavailable in this fixture
resolvedFacts.consequence: invasive-extraction and fault-injection resistance are left false rather than inferred from the register readout

alternatives: treating every image decision as board-observed
resolvedFacts.decision: only current@7 is board-observed as executing; every other image decision is simulation
resolvedFacts.consequence: the negative and recovery paths are state-machine outcomes, not measurements taken on hardware

minimumVersionDemonstration.conclusion: the minimum-version resolution is what turns the signed older image from an accepted downgrade into a rollback rejection; the counterfactual policy shows the same image booting

capabilities.description: the device talks to a fleet service over an authenticated channel; an attacker can reach the endpoint but the device still enforces image authenticity, product binding and version state locally
the fleet, update and provisioning channels are reachable by anyone who can complete the protocol handshake; capability is what the fleet record grants, not protocol reachability
the board can be held on a bench with SWD, UART and ROM download pads reachable; the fixture contract asks for authority under exactly this state
an attacker can keep the board and factory-reset it, then try to bring it back into the fleet; this is the state the fleet revocation check must defeat
no removable media surface is recorded for this board class; recorded as an explicit absence rather than left unexamined
clock, voltage and glitch attacks are a real capability for this attacker class, and none of them were exercised in this fixture
programming-time access could install a different key-hash anchor or lower version state; the key-hash fuse record is the control and its physical enforcement was not exercised here

consequences.trigger: the per-device credential is readable or exportable through a debug or download interface
consequences.control: non-exportable hardware-backed slot, production lock register observed on the board, fleet rotation and revocation

consequences.trigger: a revoked, reset or decommissioned device regains fleet authorization
consequences.control: fleet revocation keyed to the immutable device identity, checked on recovery and on reprovisioning; a local reset cannot clear it

consequences.trigger: an unsigned, corrupt, wrong-product or downgraded image is executed
consequences.control: signature, integrity, product and protected-version checks reject before execution; recovery is a separate authorization

consequences.trigger: a device in a safety-relevant role runs firmware that was never authorized for that product
consequences.control: product binding plus the authenticated boot chain; the boot gate is enforced before any actuating code runs

consequences.trigger: device identity or credential material is extracted and used to link or impersonate a device
consequences.control: no interface returns key material; the credential signs challenges and never leaves the slot

consequences.trigger: an interrupted update leaves the device with no bootable slot
consequences.control: the A/B update state machine keeps the previously authenticated slot selected before commit

productionLockState.observation: corpus records observed.productionLockRegister=true for board mcu-rev-c; the register value is therefore hardware-observed
enforces: SWD cannot perform unrestricted firmware or secret readout
only the explicitly authenticated recovery path remains
ROM download authority is bounded by the same boot gate as an ordinary update
notEstablished: that the register is physically tamper-proof
that the debug lock survives decapsulation, voltage glitching or a fault attack
that the register cannot be rewritten by a programming-time attacker

interfaceAuthority.grammar: <state>:<privilege>; state is one of normal or physical-possession, and a no- privilege prefix records an explicit denial. The authored policy is .kory-eval/device-config.json.

states.normal: device operating in the owner's possession: no attacker access to the board
states.physical-possession: attacker has temporary physical possession: board desoldered or case opened, SWD/UART/ROM pads reachable, no credentials, no persistent firmware write authority

model.deviceIdentity: immutable device-x:mcu-rev-c:0007; a factory reset never deletes it, because fleet revocation is keyed to it
model.fleetRecord: device identity, provisioned/revoked/decommissioned state, active credential id and revocation list
model.authority: local authority and fleet authority are separate: a device can hold a credential it is not allowed to use

rotateAndRevoke.rotation: explicit rotate semantics: the new credential lands in the slot and the previous credential id is revoked at the fleet in the same operation
rotateAndRevoke.revocation: explicit revoke semantics: the active credential id moves to the fleet revocation list and the device holds only stale local authority
rotateAndRevoke.backup: no backup of the credential exists: the slot is the only copy and it is not exportable

transcript.access: manufacturing station with station credentials
transcript.enforcedBy: credential generated inside the hardware-backed slot, never written as plaintext
transcript.reason: per-device credential provisioned into the non-exportable hardware-backed slot; the fleet record registers the immutable device identity and the credential id

transcript.access: device in normal operation against the fleet service
transcript.enforcedBy: slot binding + fleet record agreement
transcript.reason: fleet service accepts the device: credential present, non-exportable and matching the fleet record

transcript.access: physical-possession + debug interface, SWD readout
transcript.enforcedBy: non-exportable hardware-backed slot
transcript.reason: the slot is hardware-backed and marked non-exportable: no interface returns key material, only a signature over a supplied challenge

transcript.access: fleet-initiated rotation while the device is in the owner's possession
transcript.enforcedBy: rotate semantics: the new credential lands in the slot and the previous credential id is revoked at the fleet in the same operation
transcript.reason: rotated cred-v1 to cred-v2; the previous credential id joins the fleet revocation list

transcript.access: attacker presents the rotated-out credential cred-v1
transcript.enforcedBy: fleet revocation list + slot binding
transcript.reason: a rotated-out credential refuses on the fleet service; holding a retired credential id grants nothing

transcript.access: fleet update channel, signed and product-bound candidate
transcript.enforcedBy: the update path never touches the credential slot
transcript.reason: application slot updated through the authenticated A/B path; the credential slot still holds the same non-exportable credential, so the credential survives update

transcript.access: physical-possession, authenticated recovery entry over SWD/UART/ROM USB
transcript.enforcedBy: separate recovery authorization + fleet revocation check
transcript.reason: separate recovery authorization present and the fleet record authorizes the device

transcript.access: physical-possession, recovery image without the separate authorization
transcript.enforcedBy: separate recovery authorization
transcript.reason: recovery is a separately authorized destination: a valid image signature alone does not open it

transcript.access: physical-possession, SWD memory read of firmware and secrets
transcript.enforcedBy: production lock register observed on the representative board
transcript.reason: the production lock register read on the board keeps SWD from unrestricted firmware/secret readout; only the explicitly authenticated recovery path remains

transcript.access: owner-initiated factory reset, or an attacker resetting a board they possess
transcript.enforcedBy: reset destroys credential authority in the slot while the fleet record keeps the immutable device identity
transcript.reason: local credential authority destroyed: the hardware-backed slot is zeroized. The fleet record keeps tracking the immutable device identity, and a device the fleet refused stays refused across the reset

transcript.access: reset device tries to resume fleet operations without re-provisioning
transcript.enforcedBy: local credential authority is none after reset and the fleet record is not provisioned
transcript.reason: no credential present in the hardware-backed slot; this is the partial state the contract is about: the local slot is empty while the fleet record still lists the device

transcript.access: authorized fleet channel presenting an authenticated reprovision ticket
transcript.enforcedBy: reprovision requires an authenticated authorization, not local state
transcript.reason: authorized reprovision installs a fresh credential cred-v3; the destroyed credential is never resurrected, so only the new credential id is live

transcript.access: fleet operator revokes the device (compromise, loss, return)
transcript.enforcedBy: revoke semantics: the active credential id moves to the fleet revocation list
transcript.reason: fleet record moves to revoked and the active credential id joins the revocation list; the device keeps a local copy it can no longer use, which is stale authority

transcript.access: attacker factory-resets the revoked board and tries to reprovision with fleet authority
transcript.enforcedBy: fleet revocation is keyed to the immutable device identity, so a local reset cannot clear it

keysAndCounters.rotation: explicit rotate semantics: the new credential lands in the slot and the previous credential id is revoked at the fleet in the same operation

keysAndCounters.backup: no backup of the credential exists: the slot is the only copy and it is not exportable

limits: The credential lifecycle is this repository's own model, not silicon: it shows which transitions are reachable and which moves are refused, not how a real slot behaves under a probing attack.

The production lock register value is board-observed (corpus observed.productionLockRegister=true); what it physically enforces is not, because the corpus records debugLockProof=false and physicalFuseProof=false.
Interface authority is the authored production policy in .kory-eval/device-config.json. It is documentation, and each attempt in this artifact is re-derived from that policy rather than measured.
The boot, rollback and power-cut outcomes are simulator behaviour. Real power-fail behaviour, flash wear and partial erase are not modelled.
Image digests are content digests of the corpus image records, not measurements of flash contents on hardware.
Only the current image is recorded as executing on the board; the negative and recovery paths were not flashed in this fixture.
No fleet backend was available in this environment, so revocation, rotation and reprovisioning are demonstrated against the model, not against a live service.
No fault-injection, invasive or side-channel work was performed, and none of those resistances are claimed.

supportedByThisFixture: the production lock register is observed on the representative board and the policy keeps SWD from unrestricted firmware/secret readout, with the authenticated recovery path as the remaining route
60 interface attempts were re-derived from the authored policy with the supplied interfaceCan(); 55 are refused and the 5 grants are the read-only boot log and the authenticated recovery entry
the board-observed current image (current@7) boots and is the only image recorded as executing on hardware
unsigned, corrupt, wrong-product and signed-older fixtures are all rejected before execution in the state machine
every power-cut transition in 9 scenarios recovers to an authenticated current, candidate or authorized-recovery slot
recovery requires the separate authorization: removing it turns the same signed recovery image into a rollback rejection

the credential lifecycle transcript runs 21 steps: provisioning, non-exportable use, rotation with the previous credential revoked, survival through update, authorized recovery, reset, silent-reauthorization refusal, revocation, reset-after-revocation refusal, RMA reprovision and decommission
factory reset destroys local credential authority while the fleet record keeps the immutable device identity, so a reset device cannot silently regain authorization
fleet revocation is checked on recovery, so a refused device stays refused across a reset and across the recovery path

physical fuse enforcement and resistance to physical secret extraction: the corpus records emulator.physicalFuseProof=false
invasive-extraction and fault-injection resistance: not exercised and therefore not claimed
that the production lock register is tamper-proof or that resetting the board clears it: neither was attempted here
anything about real flash contents: image digests are digests of corpus records
claims.claimBoundary: This artifact shows the interface authority policy, the credential lifecycle state machine, and the boot/rollback/power-cut state machine. Debug-lock enforcement, physical fuse enforcement, resistance to invasive extraction, fault-injection resistance and real power-fail behaviour are outside what this fixture can show.
